QuestionText: Which of the following is an ACTION word (Verb)?
Explanation: 'Jump' is a verb — an action you can do. You can jump! 'Beautiful' and 'Blue' describe, 'Apple' is a naming word.

QuestionText: Which of the following is an ACTION word (Verb)?
Explanation: 'Run' is a verb — it is an action. You run in the playground! 'Happy' and 'Fast' describe, 'Red' is a colour.

QuestionText: Which of the following is an ACTION word (Verb)?
Explanation: 'Swim' is a verb — it is an action. Fish and people swim in water! 'Tall', 'Big', and 'Green' all describe.

QuestionText: Which of the following is an ACTION word (Verb)?
Explanation: 'Eat' is a verb — an action you do three times a day! 'Sweet', 'Tasty', and 'Hot' all describe.

QuestionText: Which of the following is an ACTION word (Verb)?
Explanation: 'Sing' is a verb — it is an action. You sing songs! 'Loud', 'Musical', and 'Pretty' are describing words.

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: The rabbit ___ very fast across the field.
Explanation: 'Runs' is the action word (verb). The rabbit runs fast! The other words describe, not act.

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: The children ___ in the park every evening.
Explanation: 'Play' is the action word (verb). The children play in the park — that is something they DO!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: She ___ a sandwich for her lunch.
Explanation: 'Cooked' is the action word (verb). Cooking is what she did to make the sandwich!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: The baby ___ when it is hungry.
Explanation: 'Cries' is the action word (verb). The baby cries to tell you it is hungry!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: Tom ___ to school every morning.
Explanation: 'Walks' is the action word (verb). Tom walks to school — walking is the action he does!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: The dog ___ at strangers who come to the door.
Explanation: 'Barks' is the action word (verb). A dog barks when it sees a stranger — woof woof!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: My mother ___ a delicious dinner for us every night.
Explanation: 'Cooks' is the action word (verb). Your mother cooks food — cooking is the action she does!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: The birds ___ south when winter comes.
Explanation: 'Fly' is the action word (verb). Birds fly — they flap their wings and soar through the sky!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: Father ___ the newspaper after dinner.
Explanation: 'Reads' is the action word (verb). Reading is what father does — he looks at the words in the newspaper!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: We ___ songs together in the music class.
Explanation: 'Sing' is the action word (verb). In music class, you sing songs — singing is the action!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: The fish ___ happily in the clear pond.
Explanation: 'Swims' is the action word (verb). A fish swims in water — that is how it moves around!

QuestionText: Choose the correct action word: The sun ___ brightly in the blue sky.
Explanation: 'Shines' is the action word (verb). The sun shines — it gives out bright light every day!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: I ___ a student.
Explanation: We use 'am' with 'I'. Always say: 'I am a student.' Remember: I → am!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: They ___ my best friends.
Explanation: We use 'are' with 'They'. Say: 'They are my best friends.' Remember: they/we/you → are!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: She ___ a very good dancer.
Explanation: We use 'is' with 'She'. Say: 'She is a good dancer.' Remember: he/she/it → is!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: We ___ playing in the garden right now.
Explanation: We use 'are' with 'We'. Say: 'We are playing in the garden.' Remember: we/you/they → are!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: He ___ a kind and helpful doctor.
Explanation: We use 'is' with 'He'. Say: 'He is a kind doctor.' Remember: he/she/it → is!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: You ___ very clever indeed!
Explanation: We use 'are' with 'You'. Say: 'You are very clever!' Remember: you → are!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: The cat ___ sleeping on the sofa.
Explanation: We use 'is' with 'The cat' (it). Say: 'The cat is sleeping.' Remember: he/she/it → is!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: The dogs ___ playing in the park.
Explanation: We use 'are' with 'The dogs' (plural). Say: 'The dogs are playing.' Plural things → are!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: I ___ very happy today.
Explanation: We use 'am' with 'I'. Say: 'I am very happy today.' Remember: I → am!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: My sister ___ five years old.
Explanation: We use 'is' with 'My sister' (she). Say: 'My sister is five years old.' Remember: she → is!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: The flowers ___ beautiful in the garden.
Explanation: We use 'are' with 'The flowers' (plural). Say: 'The flowers are beautiful.' Plural things → are!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: Tom and Jerry ___ good friends.
Explanation: We use 'are' for two people. Tom and Jerry = they, so we say 'They are good friends.'

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: The baby ___ sleeping in the crib.
Explanation: We use 'is' for 'The baby' (singular/it). Say: 'The baby is sleeping in the crib.'

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: My hands ___ very cold today.
Explanation: We use 'are' for 'My hands' (plural). Say: 'My hands are cold.' Two hands = plural → are!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: The sky ___ bright blue today.
Explanation: We use 'is' for 'The sky' (singular/it). Say: 'The sky is bright blue today.'

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: My parents ___ very kind and loving.
Explanation: We use 'are' for 'My parents' (plural). Two parents = plural → are!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: I ___ six years old and I go to Grade One.
Explanation: We use 'am' with 'I'. Always say: 'I am six years old.' I → am!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: ___ elephant is the largest land animal.
Explanation: We use 'An' before a vowel sound. 'Elephant' starts with 'E' (a vowel), so we say 'An elephant'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: I have ___ dog named Max.
Explanation: We use 'a' before a consonant sound. 'Dog' starts with 'D' (a consonant), so we say 'a dog'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: Please close ___ door when you leave.
Explanation: 'The' is used for a specific thing both the speaker and listener know about. 'The door' means a particular door.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: She ate ___ apple for her snack.
Explanation: We use 'an' before a vowel sound. 'Apple' starts with 'A' (a vowel), so we say 'an apple'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: I saw ___ bird sitting in the mango tree.
Explanation: We use 'a' before a consonant sound. 'Bird' starts with 'B' (a consonant), so we say 'a bird'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: The teacher opened ___ book and began to read.
Explanation: 'The' refers to a specific book — the one the teacher is holding. 'The book' = a particular, known book.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: He is ___ honest and hardworking boy.
Explanation: We use 'an' before a vowel sound. 'Honest' has a silent H, so it sounds like it starts with 'O'. We say 'an honest boy'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: We live very near ___ big river.
Explanation: We use 'a' before a consonant sound. 'Big river' — 'big' starts with 'B' (a consonant), so 'a big river'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: Look at ___ moon tonight — it is so round and bright!
Explanation: We use 'the' for unique things. There is only one moon, so we always say 'the moon'!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: She wants ___ ice cream from the shop.
Explanation: We use 'an' before a vowel sound. 'Ice cream' starts with 'I' (a vowel), so we say 'an ice cream'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: My father is ___ engineer who builds bridges.
Explanation: We use 'an' before a vowel sound. 'Engineer' starts with 'E' (a vowel), so we say 'an engineer'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: ___ sun rises in the east every morning.
Explanation: We use 'The' for unique things. There is only one sun, so we always say 'The sun'!

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: I need ___ umbrella because it is raining!
Explanation: We use 'an' before a vowel sound. 'Umbrella' starts with 'U' (a vowel), so we say 'an umbrella'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: The baby is eating ___ orange after lunch.
Explanation: We use 'an' before a vowel sound. 'Orange' starts with 'O' (a vowel), so we say 'an orange'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: She has ___ pet cat that she loves very much.
Explanation: We use 'a' before a consonant sound. 'Pet' starts with 'P' (a consonant), so we say 'a pet cat'.

QuestionText: Fill in the blank: The children went to ___ zoo on a school trip.
Explanation: We use 'the' for a specific, well-known place. The children went to 'the zoo' — a particular zoo they all know.
